farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أَفَنَضْرِبُ عَنكُمُ ٱلذِّكْرَ صَفْحاً أَن كُنتُمْ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash read: "إن كنتم" with kasra, and ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥasan read: "أنْ كنتم" with fatḥa on (أنْ), as though they meant something past. In ordinary speech you say: "Shall I revile you أن you deprived me?", meaning "since (إذ) you deprived me"; and you use kasra when you mean: "Shall I revile you if (إن) you deprive me?" Like it is: ﴿ولاَ يَجْرِمَنّكُمْ شَنآنُ قَوْمٍ أَنْ صَدُّوكم﴾: you may read (إن) with kasra or with fatḥa.
And like it: ﴿فلعلَّك باخعٌ نفسك على آثارِهم﴾ "إن لم يؤمنوا" and "أن لم يؤمنوا". The Arabs recite the saying of al-Farazdaq:
أتجزع إن أذنا قتيبة حزتا * جهاراً، ولم تجزع لقتل ابن خازم؟
(Do you grieve if [or: that] the two ears of Qutayba were cut off openly, yet you did not grieve at the killing of Ibn Khāzim?)
And they recited to me:
أتجزع أن بان الخليط المودّع * وجبل الصفا من عزة المتقطع؟
(Do you grieve that the departing companions have parted, and the bond of affection with ʿAzza that is cut?)
And in each of the two verses there is what is in its companion: kasra and fatḥa. And the Arabs say: "I have turned away (أضربت) from you" and "I turned (ضربت) from you", when they mean by it: I left you and I turned aside from you.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿لِتَسْتَوُواْ عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِ﴾.
Someone may say: how did He say "على ظهوره" (on its backs), attaching "backs" to a singular? It is said to him: that singular is in the meaning of a plural, in the same way as "the troops", "the army" and "the whole body". If he says: then why did you not say "لتستووا على ظهره" (on its back), making "back" singular when you attach it to a singular? I say: the singular contains the meaning of the plural, so I returned "backs" to the meaning and did not say "its back", lest it be like the singular whose meaning and wording are both singular. Likewise you say: "The women of the troops (الجند) have become many", and you say: "The troops raised their eyes (أعينه)", and do not say "its eye (عينه)". And likewise everything you attach to such of the concrete nouns, you bring out in the plural; but when you attach to it a noun in the meaning of an action (fiʿl), both its plural and its singular are allowed, as in your saying: "The troops raised their voice (صوته)" and "their voices (أصواته)", which is better. This is allowed because the action has no form in the dual other than its form in the singular.
His saying: ﴿وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ﴾.
Capable of it (muṭīqīn). You say to a man: "You have become مُقرن for this", i.e. you are capable of it and have become a match (qirn) for it.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدّاً﴾.
The verb belongs to the face, so for that reason you put the predicate (fiʿl) in the accusative; and had you made "ظلّ" belong to the man, you would put "the face" and "blackened" in the nominative, saying: ظل وجهه مسودٌّ وهو كظيم.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿أَوَمَن يُنَشَّأُ فِي ٱلْحِلْيَةِ﴾.
He means the females. He says: you have assigned daughters to the All-Merciful, while you are such that when a daughter is born to one of you, what He described befalls him. As for His saying ﴿أومَنْ﴾, it is as though He said: "and one who is not brought up except in ornaments, and who in dispute is not clear", i.e. does not attain in argument what a man attains. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "أَوَمَنْ لا يُنَشَّأُ إلاّ فى الْحِلْيَةِ". If you wish [169/b], you put "مَن" in the position of the nominative by resumption (istiʾnāf); and if you wish, you put it in the accusative by an implied verb, "they make (يجعلون)" or the like; and if you refer it back to the beginning of the speech, to His saying: "وإِذَ بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُمْ بِما ضَرَبَ", you put it in the genitive [and if you wish, in the accusative]. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, the companions of ʿAbd Allāh and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read: "يُنَشَّأُ", and ʿĀṣim and the people of the Ḥijāz read: ينْشَأُ فى الحلية.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿عِبَادُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, ʿAlqama and the companions of ʿAbd Allāh read it: "عباد الرحمن"; and it is reported [of] ʿUmar (may Allah have mercy on him) that he read it: "عند الرحمن", and likewise ʿĀṣim and the people of the Ḥijāz, as though they took that from His saying: ﴿إنَّ الذين عِنْد رَبِّك لا يَسْتَكْبِرُون عَنْ عِبادَتهِ﴾. All is correct.
His saying: ﴿أَشَهِدُواْ خَلْقَهُمْ﴾.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash gave the alif of "أشهدوا" fatḥa, and the people of the Ḥijāz gave it ḍamma, in the interpretation: أُشْهدوا خلقهم ("were they made to witness their creation?"), because its agent is not named; and the meaning is the same. They read it without hamza, intending the question. Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: so al-Farrāʾ said.

farraa:22-23.t:
His saying: ﴿بَلْ قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّا وَجَدْنَآ آبَآءَنَا عَلَىٰ أُمَّةٍ﴾.
The readers read it with ḍamma on the alif of "أُمّة", and Mujāhid and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz read it with kasra. It is as though al-imma is like sunna (custom) and milla (creed); and al-imma is the way (ṭarīqa), and the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "I led (amamtu) the people". The Arabs say: "How fine is his imma, his ʿimma and his jilsa!", when it is a maṣdar. Al-imma is also dominion and bliss. ʿAdī said:
ثم بعْدَ الفلاحِ والمُلكِ والإمّة * وارثهمُ هناك القبورُ
(Then, after prosperity, dominion and imma, the graves there have concealed them.)
As though he meant the leadership of dominion and its bliss.
«[Translator's note: «وارثهم» as printed is translated by its evident sense "concealed them" (cf. واراهم); the verse is cited elsewhere as «وارتهم».]»
His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰ آثَارِهِم مُّهْتَدُونَ﴾ and ﴿مُّقْتَدُونَ﴾.
They are nominative; had they been accusative, that would have been allowed, because stopping before them is good. So you say to a man: "You came while we were following the track (متبعين / متبعون)".

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّنِي بَرَآءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ﴾.
The Arabs say: "We are barāʾ and khalāʾ of you" (quit of you); and for the singular, the dual and the plural, feminine and masculine, one says: barāʾ, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). Had He said (برىء), one would say in the dual: بريئان, and of a group: بريئون and برءاء. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: "إنَّنى بَرِئٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُون"; and had a reader read it so, it would be correct and in agreement with our reading [i.e. our codex], because the Arabs write يستهزىء as يستهزأ, writing the hamza with alif in all its states. They write شىء as شيأ, and the like is frequent in the codices of ʿAbd Allāh; and in our codex: ويهيىء لكم is written ويهيأ, with alif.

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةً بَاقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ﴾.
[It is] the name of Islam. He says: binding on whoever followed him and was of his offspring; perhaps the people of Mecca will follow this religion, since they are of the offspring of Abraham, Allah bless him. That is His saying: ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾: to your religion and the religion of Abraham, Allah bless them both.

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿لَوْلاَ نُزِّلَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنُ عَلَىٰ رَجُلٍ مِّنَ ٱلْقَرْيَتَيْنِ عَظِيمٍ﴾.
Its meaning is: on one of two men; he meant himself and Abū Masʿūd al-Thaqafī. It was al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī who said this. The two towns are Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif.

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿وَرَفَعْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَاتٍ﴾.
So We raised the master above his slave, and made some of them take others captive, so the slave and the one taken captive are made subservient to those above them.
His saying: ﴿لِّيَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُهُم بَعْضاً سُخْرِيّاً﴾, and "سِخْرِيّاً": they are one here and in "قد أفلح" [al-Muʾminūn] and in Ṣād; kasra and ḍamma in them are the same, two dialects.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ أَن يَكُونَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾.
أن is in the position of the nominative.
His saying: ﴿لَّجَعَلْنَا لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بِٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ﴾.
If you wish, you make the lām repeated in لبيوتهم, as He said: ﴿يسَأَلُونكَ عن الشَّهرِ الْحَرامِ قِتَالٍ فيه﴾; and if you wish, you make the two lāms different, as though the second were in the meaning of على, as though He said: "We would have made for them, on (على) their houses, roofs". And you say to a man to his face: "I made for you, for your people, the gifts", i.e. I made it for your sake for them.
And (السُّقُف): ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and al-Ḥasan read it "سُقُفاً". If you wish, you make its singular saqīfa, and if you wish, you make it [the plural of] suqūf, so it is a plural of a plural, as the poet said:
حتى بلت حلاقيم الحُلُق * أهوى لأدْنى فقرة على شفق
(Until the throats of the throats [ḥuluq, plural of ḥalq] were worn out, he plunged to the nearest vertebra, with apprehension.)
And like it is the reading of whoever read "كُلوُا مِن ثُمُرِه", which is a plural whose singular is thimār; and like the saying of whoever read: "فَرُهُنٌ مَقْبوضَة", whose singular is rihān and ruhūn. Mujāhid and some of the people of the Ḥijāz read ﴿سَقْفاً﴾ like the singular, lightened, because saqf has the sense of a collective.
«[Translator's note: the verse is obscure as transmitted; the gloss is tentative.]»

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿وَزُخْرُفاً﴾.
It is gold. It came in the exegesis: "We would make them for them of silver and of zukhruf". If you drop the من from الزخرف, you put it in the accusative by the verb, making it fall on it, i.e. "and zukhruf", We would make that for them of it. Others said: "and We would make for them, besides that, gold and wealth (غنى, shortened)", and it is the more likely of the two views to be correct.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَعْشُ عَن ذِكْرِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ﴾.
He means: whoever turns away from it; and whoever read it: "ومن يَعْشَ عن" means: whoever is blind to it.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَصُدُّونَهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾.
He means the devil, and it is in [170/b] the sense of a plural, though it was uttered as a singular. He says: the devils turn them away from the path, and they think that they are rightly guided.

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَآءَنَا قَالَ يٰلَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ ٱلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ﴾.
So one says: (جاءنا) for one of the two, while the human and his companion came to Us. ʿĀṣim, al-Sulamī and al-Ḥasan read it جاءانا, in the dual; and the companions of ʿAbd Allāh, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd al-Nakhaʿī, read (جاءنا) in the singular, and that is a case where one of two suffices for both. Like it is the reading of whoever read ﴿كَلاَّ لَيُنْبَذَانِّ﴾: he says: he and his wealth will be thrown; and (ولَيُنبّذَنَّ), and the meaning is the same.
«[Translator's note: «فيقتل» at the start of this paragraph is evidently a corruption (perhaps of «فيقال», "so one says"); translated accordingly.]»
His saying: ﴿يٰلَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ ٱلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ﴾.
He means: what lies between the winter sunrise and the summer sunrise. It is also said that He meant the east and the west, and said "the two easts"; and this is the more likely of the two views to be correct, because the Arabs may combine two nouns under the name of the better known of them. So one says: "The two Zahdams have come to you", while only one of them is Zahdam. The poet said:
أخذنا بآفاق السماء عليكمُ * لنا قمراها والنجوم الطوالع
(We have taken the horizons of the sky against you: ours are its two moons and the rising stars.)
He means: the sun and the moon.
And another said:
قسموا البلاد فما بها لمقيلهم * تضغيث مفتصل يباع فصيله فقرى العراق مسير يوم واحد * فالبصرتان فواسط تكميله
(They divided the lands … the towns of Iraq are a single day's journey, then the two Baṣras, then Wāsiṭ completes it.)
He means: Baṣra and Kūfa.
«[Translator's note: the first half of this poetry is obscure as transmitted and is left unglossed.]»
He said: and a man of Ṭayyiʾ recited to me:
فبصرة الأزد منا، والعراق لنا * والموصلان ومنا مصر فالحرم
(The Baṣra of the Azd is ours, and Iraq is ours, and the two Mawṣils, and Egypt is ours, then the Sanctuary.)
He means: al-Jazīra and al-Mawṣil.

farraa:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَن يَنفَعَكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ إِذ ظَّلَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ فِي ٱلْعَذَابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ﴾.
He says: your sharing will not benefit you, meaning [the devil] and his companion. And أنكم is in the position of the nominative.

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَذِكْرٌ لَّكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ﴾.
An honour for you and for your people, meaning: the Qurʾān and the religion; and you will be asked about thanks for it.

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿وَسْئَلْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾.
Someone may say: how was he commanded to ask messengers who had passed away? There are two views on it. One of them: that he ask the people of the Torah and the Gospel, for they only inform him of the Books of the messengers that they brought; so if he [asks] the Books, it is as though he asked the prophets.
And some said: you will be taken on a night journey, O Muḥammad, and meet the prophets, so ask them about that. But he, Allah bless him, did not doubt and did not ask them.
His saying: [171/a] ﴿أَجَعَلْنَا مِن دُونِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ آلِهَةً يُعْبَدُونَ﴾.
He said: ﴿يُعبَدون﴾ (masculine plural, as for rational beings) of the gods, and did not say تعبد; and they are called يُعْبَدون because the gods are spoken to, called upon and exalted, so they were treated in the same way as kings, princes and their like.
«[Translator's note: «ولم يقل: تعبد ولا يُعْبَدون» is awkward as transmitted; translated by the evident sense.]»

farraa:48-48.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا نُرِيِهِم مِّنْ آيَةٍ إِلاَّ هِيَ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ أُخْتِهَا﴾.
He means: than the sign that passed before it.

farraa:52-52.t:
His saying: ﴿أَمْ أَنَآ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ هَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينٌ﴾.
It is of the question that is made with أم because of its connection with speech before it; and if you wish, you refer it back to His saying: ﴿أَلَيْسَ لى مُلْكُ مِصْرَ﴾.
[Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: one of the shaykhs informed me, I think it was al-Kisāʾī, that it had reached him that one of the readers read: "أَمَا أنا خير"; and the shaykh said to me: "Had I preserved the report about it, I would have read it so"; and it is good in meaning.

farraa:53-53.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلَوْلاَ أُلْقِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَسْوِرَةٌ مِّن ذَهَبٍ﴾.
He means: why have bracelets of gold not been cast upon him? Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it "أساورة من ذهب", and so did the people of Medina; and it is reported of al-Ḥasan: "أَسْوِرة"; and all is correct.
Whoever read "أساورة" made its singular iswār, and whoever read "اسورة", its singular is siwār. And أساورة may be the plural of أسورة, as one says in the plural of أسقية: أساقى, and in the plural of أكرع: أكارع.

farraa:54-54.t: His saying: ﴿فَٱسْتَخَفَّ قَوْمَهُ﴾: He means: he incited them (istafazzahum).

farraa:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿فَلَمَّآ آسَفُونَا﴾. He means: they angered Us.

farraa:56-56.t:
His saying: ﴿فَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ سَلَفاً﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: al-Qāsim ibn Maʿn narrated to me, from al-Aʿmash, from Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, that he read it: "سُلُفا", with ḍamma and doubled vowels; and al-Qāsim [ibn Maʿn] claimed that he heard its singular as salīf. The generality still read: "سَلَفاً".
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us that al-Aʿraj read it: "فجعلناهم سُلُفا", as though its singular were sulfa of people, i.e. a portion of people, like umma.

farraa:57-57.t:
His saying: ﴿مِنْهُ يَصِدُّونَ﴾.
[Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to me from ʿĀṣim that he abandoned يَصُدون from the reading of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and read يصِدون. (Al-Farrāʾ said:) And Abū Bakr said: ʿĀṣim narrated to me, from Abū Razīn, from Abū Yaḥyā, that Ibn ʿAbbās [171/b] read: (يَصِدون), i.e. they clamour and cry out.
And in another report: Ibn ʿAbbās met the nephew of ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr and said: "Your cousin is surely an Arab; so why does he make a mistake (yalḥan) in His saying: ﴿إذا قومك منه يصُدون﴾? It is only يصِدون." The Arabs say: يصِد and يصُد, like يشِد and يشُد, and ينمِ and ينُم from namīm (talebearing). يصدون منه and عنه are the same.
«[Translator's note: «أبى عبدالحمن» in the source is evidently Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān [al-Sulamī]; translated accordingly.]»

farraa:61-61.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَعِلْمٌ لِّلسَّاعَةِ﴾. In the reading of Ubayy: "وإنه لذكر للساعة"; and it has been narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: "وإنه لَعَلَمٌ للساعة" and (عِلْمٌ), both; and all is correct and close in meaning.

farraa:68-68.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰعِبَادِ لاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ﴾.
In the reading of the people of Medina it is: "ياعبادى", keeping the yāʾ; and ordinary speech and the reading of the generality drop the yāʾ.

farraa:71-71.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَكْوَابٍ﴾.
The kūb is the round-headed [vessel] that has no handle (ear). ʿAdī said:
خيرٌ لها إن خشيت حجرة * من ربِّها زيدٍ بن أيوبِ متكئا تصفق أبوابه * يَسقِى عليه العبد بالكوب
(Better for her, if she fears a year of drought, than her master Zayd ibn Ayyūb, reclining while his doors are clapped open and shut, the slave serving him drink with the kūb.)
His saying: ﴿تَشْتَهِى الأَنْفُس﴾: in the codices of the people of Medina: تشتهيهِ الأنفسُ وتلدُّ.

farraa:75-75.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ يُفَتَّرُ عَنْهُمْ وَهُمْ فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ﴾: in the punishment.
And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "وهُم فيها مُبلسون", referring to Jahannam. The mublis is the despairing one, hopeless of deliverance.

farraa:76-76.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا ظَلَمْنَاهُمْ وَلَـٰكِن كَانُواْ هُمُ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾.
You make (هم) here a support (ʿimād, the separating pronoun), and so الظالمين is accusative; whoever makes it a noun puts it in the nominative; and it is in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (ولكن كانُوا هُم الظَّالمون).

farraa:79-79.t:
His saying: ﴿أَمْ أَبْرَمُوۤاْ أَمْراً﴾.
He means: have they settled, in their own estimation, an affair that will save them from Our punishment? For We are settling [Our affair], punishing them.

farraa:88-88.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقِيلِهِ يٰرَبِّ﴾.
ʿĀṣim, al-Sulamī, Ḥamza and some of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh put it in the genitive, and the people of Medina and al-Ḥasan, as far as I know, put it in the accusative. Whoever puts it in the genitive says: "With Him is the knowledge of the Hour" and the knowledge of "his saying: O Lord". Whoever puts it in the accusative implies a verb of saying with it, as though He said: "and he said his saying", and complained his complaint to his Lord; and it is in one of the two readings [172/a]. Al-Farrāʾ said: I know it only in the reading of Ubayy, because I saw it in some codices of ʿAbd Allāh [as] وقيله. The accusative is also allowed from His saying: "نسمع سرهم ونجواهم", "and We hear his saying". And had someone said وقيلُه, in the nominative, it would be allowed, as you say: "and his call is this word: O Lord". Then He said: "فاصفَحْ عَنْهُمْ", connecting it to his supplication, as though it were from his saying, while it is from the command of Allah: He commanded him to pardon; He commanded him this before he was commanded to fight them.
«[Translator's note: the sentence about Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh is garbled as transmitted (a reading attributed to Ubayy is justified by ʿAbd Allāh's codices); translated literally.]»

farraa:89-89.t:
﴿وَقُلْ سَلاَمٌ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
سلام is nominative by an implied عليكم or the like; and had it been وقل سلاماً, it would have been correct, as He said: ﴿قالوا سَلاَماً قال سَلاَمٌ﴾.
